display.title: Episode 464: Three Lost on an Island, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi speaks about Hashem's hidden miracles, and the island parable ends: who deserves the king's greatest reward, and what it teaches about the neshamah.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens by speaking about the great miracles Hashem was performing to protect the Jewish people. Hashem, the Guardian of Israel, never sleeps, and many miracles go unnoticed even by the people they happen to, which is why we thank Hashem in Modim for His miracles every day. Recognizing Hashem's closeness brings simcha, and in the merit of simcha we will leave golus. After the Hakochainik march, a class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time concludes 'Three Lost on an Island'. Through the telescope the survivors see a sign at a castle: the queen is gravely ill. They fly there, and the doctor's apple cures her. All three claim the reward of marrying the princess; the king gives each riches but the princess to the doctor, because the apple stays with him. Uncle Yossi explains the parable: our body and our physical needs matter, but the greatest reward goes to the neshamah, since only Torah and good deeds accompany a person to the World to Come. The show closes with an ad for the Tzivos Hashem Jewish Family Expo.
display.lesson: The body and its needs are important, but the neshamah is what lasts forever; only Torah and mitzvos come with us to the World to Come.
